newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer after U.S. PPI data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer after U.S. PPI data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Friday boosted by weaker-than-expected U.S. producer price index data and strong momentum heading into the release of the federal budget on Tuesday, dealers said.

"It's just feeding off some good technicals and a continuing positive trend to Canada going into budget really," said a T-bill trader for one bank owned-brokerage. "The U.S. PPI number just came out too, so that sort of gives a bit of a lift to the market as well."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.83 percent from 2.84 percent at Thursday's close.
Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets were firmer after reports that the U.S. January PPI fell 0.3 percent, though markets had been trading stronger going into the data.
Dealers said a stronger Canadian dollar also provided support for T-bills. The Canadian dollar opened firmer at C$1.3500 (US$0.7407) from Thursday's close of C$1.3512 (US$0.7401).
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.05 percent from 3.08 percent at the close of trading on Thursday.
The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.31 percent from 3.34 percent.
The call loan rate or overnight lending rate traded at 2.90 percent, in the lower half of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
